checks.text: Arm links keep 21 mm or more from the egg shell, the docking port, the gel surface and the stern rim in every one of 5443 frames (10 mm asked).
Links and tool keep 9.9 mm from the boom stages (10 mm asked, met within the 0.1 mm of the sampled meshes).
The tool keeps 15 mm from the shell, the docking port and the stern rim.
Only the push tube and the needle enter the gel: the tool head stays 46 mm above the gel surface.

Around the placed kit the 6 mm push tube passes the kit parts by 2.4 mm and the needle laps 1.4 mm onto the saddle lip where the skin closes on the kit, as in the Stage 3 print; the arm and the tool head stay far off.
While the newborn is lifted, pushed and inflated, the links stay 215 mm and the tube 34 mm from the body.
Going in for the birth, the links stay 191 mm from the cured body.
The inflating body clears the shell and the stern rim by 105 mm on the way out.
Every joint stays 11 degrees or more inside the official URDF limits.
Joint speeds stay under the datasheet (J1 to J3 225 deg/s, J4 to J6 180 deg/s): highest 51 percent of the limit, while the arm goes back to the tail.
The boom carriage moves at 66 mm/s at most.
Tool tip on target in every frame: worst 0.29 mm (all 4156 G-code points included).

Push while inflating: every story stays folded inside the gel chamber until that story passes the stern rim; the first opens at 81 s, the last as the tail end leaves the rim; air is metered to the push position (peak 2.0 L/min), the push waits while the air catches up.
Lift and push stay inside the 2 kg payload: peak 7.5 N of 19.6 N (the whole body with the kit and the trapped gel, 0.76 kg, once out of the gel).
Docked egg trim: level with the arm folded, tilted 1.0 degrees with the arm at the print and 1.4 at the end of the push (stiff: 1612 N m per radian).

Tail alone, arm folded: 43.3 kg with 23.0 kg of water ballast in the keel tanks, floats level at the egg waterline (z -169 mm), so the faces meet when docking. With the arm out the tail would pitch 19 degrees, so the arm folds before every undock.
The docking port of the gel chamber stays above water when the tail is away: port bottom 29 mm over the waterline.
The stern opening is wholly above water: lowest point 19 mm over the waterline.
Click: nine magnet pairs pull the tail in over the last 20 mm; the tail meets the nine 3 mm silicone bumpers at 157 mm/s, peak 951 N in all (106 N each); the pairs then hold 157 N.
Newborn: falls 183 mm from the stern opening, enters the water at 1.7 m/s, floats with the axis 14 mm under the surface.
